newsitem.title: USA: Merrill Lynch to appeal Orange County order.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch to appeal Orange County order.

text.p: Merrill Lynch and Co said Wednesday it would appeal a California judge's decision to order the immediate release of grand jury transcripts about the firm's role in the Orange County bankruptcy.
"We disagree with the court's interpretation of the law and intend to seek an appeal," Merrill Lynch spokesman Timothy Gilles said.
He said Merrill intended to move expeditiously to appeal Orange County Superior Court Judge David Carter's ruling. The appeal would be to the California court of appeals, he said.
Earlier, in a written ruling released in Santa Ana, California, Carter ordered the immediate release of the grand jury transcripts.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy in December 1994 after losing more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy last year.

In June, Merrill Lynch settled with Orange County's district attorney for $30 million, ensuring that the brokerage giant and its employees would not face criminal charges. Transcripts of the grand jury probe have so far remained sealed.
County prosecutors and Merrill Lynch had argued that the transcripts should remain sealed because no indictments were returned by the grand jury.
